evidence.quote:
Every Meridian deployment now requires a signed release
manifest before it ships.

observations.why: Quinton enacts authority-ranking by declaring a mandatory gate — 'requires' frames a hierarchical constraint imposed on all deployments.

evidence.quote:
two unsigned artifacts reach staging
last quarter and that is the whole reason for the gate

observations.why: Quinton justifies the gate with a proportionality argument — past violations are the cost that the gate is designed to prevent, framing consequence-for-choice.

evidence.quote: signed release manifest required for Meridian deploys

observations.why: Xena records the gate as a requirement — authority-ranking enacted through a mandated precondition on deploys.
Extending the gate's jurisdiction across environments enacts authority-ranking — the rule's reach is defined hierarchically.
Assigning a named owner enacts authority-ranking — a single individual holds hierarchical responsibility for the gate.

mints.name: MandateGateAsRequirement
mints.title: a precondition stated as a non-negotiable requirement before something can proceed
mints.frame: Is the constraint here entering as a hierarchical mandate that must be satisfied before action, rather than as a preference or recommendation?
